name: Three Federal Laws in Plain English
title: Three Federal Laws in Plain English
answer: Three federal laws do most of the work of protecting students online: FERPA protects student education records, COPPA protects personal information of children under 13 on commercial websites and apps, and CIPA sets internet filtering and safety rules for schools that receive federal internet discounts. A fourth law, the Protection of Pupil Rights Amendment, gives parents rights over surveys and marketing involving their children. This matters because AI tools can touch records, children's data, filtered internet use, and sensitive student surveys, so schools need to know which law applies.

crumbs.name: Privacy, Safety, and the Human Review Rule

sections.body: The idea is that a small set of federal laws frames most student privacy and safety duties online. FERPA covers education records, COPPA covers personal information from children under 13 on commercial websites and apps, and CIPA covers internet filtering and safety in schools that receive federal discounts for internet service. The Protection of Pupil Rights Amendment adds parent rights over surveys and marketing that involve their children. The problem it solves is confusion about which rules apply when a school considers an AI tool. The text says each law gets a closer look later, with attention to how AI changes what a school must do.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: In a school or classroom, the laws apply by what the tool does and who it serves. For children under 13, COPPA focuses on personal information when they use commercial websites and apps. FERPA applies when a tool touches student education records. CIPA applies to internet filtering and safety in schools that receive federal discounts for internet service. The Protection of Pupil Rights Amendment can apply when a tool asks students about sensitive topics, and it gives parents rights over surveys and marketing involving their children.

sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: The limits come from each law's scope. FERPA is about education records, COPPA is about personal information of children under 13 on commercial websites and apps, CIPA is about internet filtering and safety in schools that receive federal discounts, and the Protection of Pupil Rights Amendment is about parent rights over surveys and marketing. The text says the fourth law matters less for most AI tools, but it can apply when a tool asks students about sensitive topics. The excerpt does not describe a human review decision or assign specific decisions to a person beyond those parent rights.
